findings.highlight: given that everything Youko-san's done has been for Kazusa's sake, she doesn't really know much about Setsuna at all.
findings.evidenceJa: 何しろ、今まで彼女がかずさのためにしてきたことは、雪菜をよく知らないからこそできたとも言える訳で。
findings.explanation: The point is causal and morally damning: Youko could do everything she did for Kazusa precisely because she did not know Setsuna well. The English states two disconnected facts and erases the implication that ignorance enabled her cruelty.
findings.japanese:
何しろ、今まで彼女がかずさのためにしてきたことは、
雪菜をよく知らないからこそできたとも言える訳で。
findings.todokanai: In any case, given that everything Youko-san's done has been for Kazusa's sake, she doesn't really know much about Setsuna at all.

findings.highlight: She feels that she's worth fighting for.
findings.evidenceJa: 目の前にいる人が、かずさと同じだって気づいたから。戦うに値する相手だって、感じ取ったから。
findings.explanation: Setsuna recognizes Youko as like Kazusa—an opponent worthy of fighting. 'Worth fighting for' makes Youko a beneficiary whom Setsuna wishes to defend, reversing the combative relationship.
findings.japanese:
目の前にいる人が、かずさと同じだって気づいたから。
戦うに値する相手だって、感じ取ったから。
findings.todokanai: She's realized that the person before her is very similar to Kazusa. She feels that she's worth fighting for.

findings.highlight: I like you, Kazusa! Is me liking you not a good enough reason, Kazusa!?
findings.evidenceJa: 「好きだから！かずさのこと、大好きだからじゃいけないの！？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna escalates from 好き to 大好き: she loves Kazusa dearly and asks why that cannot justify staying. The English flattens both to 'like,' repeating the same weakening at line 284 despite the scene's explicit like/love/hate vocabulary.
findings.japanese:
「好きだから！
かずさのこと、大好きだからじゃいけないの！？」
findings.todokanai: "I like you, Kazusa! Is me liking you not a good enough reason, Kazusa!?"

findings.highlight: Who ever decided that it's impossible to like horrible people?
findings.evidenceJa: 「最低な人を好きになっちゃいけないなんて、一体誰が決めたのよ！？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks who decided one must not love a terrible person—a challenge to moral prohibition. The English asks who decided it is impossible, collapsing her ethical defense into a factual argument about capacity.
findings.japanese:
「最低な人を好きになっちゃいけないなんて、
一体誰が決めたのよ！？」
findings.todokanai: "Who ever decided that it's impossible to like horrible people?"

findings.highlight: As Setsuna momentarily left to plant the flower she'd brought
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜が花を生けるために席を外すと、曜子さんは、なんだか呆れたような視線で俺を見上げた。
findings.explanation: Setsuna steps away to arrange the cut flowers in a vase. The English says she leaves to plant the moth orchid inside a hospital, producing a physically and culturally wrong action.
findings.japanese:
雪菜が花を生けるために席を外すと、
曜子さんは、なんだか呆れたような視線で俺を見上げた。
findings.todokanai: As Setsuna momentarily left to plant the flower she'd brought, Youko-san suddenly stared at me with a bewildered expression for some reason.

findings.highlight: The client which we're giving our proposal to is currently in the hospital. And the person who's giving that proposal hasn't really gone through any of the official procedures required; instead, he simply rode on the fact that Youko-san's the mother of her friend to push it upon her.
findings.evidenceJa:
売り込むべきクライアントは入院中。
しかも、何一つ正式な段取りを踏まずに、
ただ、友達の母親というコネを利用しただけのゴリ押し。
findings.explanation: The source describes the proposal as a brute-force use of a friend's-mother connection; the English assigns the presentation to a male 'he,' despite Setsuna delivering it and the pair devising it — Their joint authorship and Haruki's role in obtaining access are both established.
findings.japanese:
売り込むべきクライアントは入院中。
しかも、何一つ正式な段取りを踏まずに、
ただ、友達の母親というコネを利用しただけのゴリ押し。
findings.todokanai: The client which we're giving our proposal to is currently in the hospital. And the person who's giving that proposal hasn't really gone through any of the official procedures required; instead, he simply rode on the fact that Youko-san's the mother of her friend to push it upon her.

findings.highlight: for a girl who's trying to take back the man she loves?
findings.evidenceJa: 「普通、ここまでする？ふった女のために。自分の彼にコナかけてくる女のために」
findings.explanation: Youko asks whether anyone would go this far for a woman her boyfriend rejected who is now making a pass at that boyfriend. The English says Kazusa is trying to 'take back' the man she loves, granting her prior ownership and removing Setsuna's relationship boundary.
findings.japanese:
「普通、ここまでする？
ふった女のために。
自分の彼にコナかけてくる女のために」
findings.todokanai: "Would someone usually go so far? For a girl you rejected… for a girl who's trying to take back the man she loves?"

findings.explanation: Haruki answers personally: Kazusa is someone important to him. The English pluralizes this into 'important to us,' diffusing his continuing individual attachment into the joint rescue project.

findings.highlight: I imagine only Kazusa would forgive me in such a scenario…
findings.evidenceJa: かずさだけは、許すって…
findings.explanation: In context Haruki recognizes that Setsuna, unlike Youko or Haruki, would forgive Kazusa alone. The English instead says Kazusa alone would forgive Haruki, reversing both forgiver and forgiven at the pivot that demonstrates Setsuna's exceptional choice.
findings.japanese: かずさだけは、許すって…
findings.todokanai: I imagine only Kazusa would forgive me in such a scenario…

findings.highlight: now the president of the company Setsuna's working at.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ええ、知ってました。その時の担当が、今の彼女の部署の部長です」
findings.explanation: The former contact is now head of Setsuna's department, not president of Knights Records. The English inflates a departmental manager into the company's chief executive and distorts the internal approval route.
findings.japanese:
「ええ、知ってました。
その時の担当が、今の彼女の部署の部長です」
findings.todokanai: "Yes, I know about that. The person responsible for that arrangement is now the president of the company Setsuna's working at."

findings.highlight: you've even looked up on how you'd manage to persuade me
findings.evidenceJa: 「既に話を通すルートまで見つけてあるんだ…抜け目ないわね」
findings.explanation: Youko notes that Haruki has already found a channel through which to get the proposal approved inside Knights. The English says he researched how to persuade Youko herself, even though he is already negotiating directly with her.
findings.japanese:
「既に話を通すルートまで見つけてあるんだ…
抜け目ないわね」
findings.todokanai: "I see you've even looked up on how you'd manage to persuade me… you let nothing slip by you, now, do you?"

findings.highlight: I suppose I can buy some time and… that's it!
findings.evidenceJa: 「じゃあ間を取って………これで！今約束できるギリギリの線です！」
findings.explanation: Haruki proposes splitting the difference between their circulation numbers and names the maximum he can presently promise. The English turns 間を取って into buying time, breaking the numerical bargaining joke.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあ間を取って………これで！
今約束できるギリギリの線です！」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I suppose I can buy some time and… that's it! That's the most I can promise you right now!"

findings.highlight: is our relationship not simple enough to be described with words like that?
findings.evidenceJa: 「好きとか、嫌いとか、愛してるとか、憎いとか…そんなふうに、十文字以内で答えられるほど、わたしたちの関係、単純じゃないのかな…？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna wonders whether their relationship is too complex to answer in ten Japanese characters or fewer with labels like like, hate, love, loathe. The English retains generic complexity but drops the precise ten-character conceit that foregrounds language's insufficiency.
findings.japanese:
「好きとか、嫌いとか、愛してるとか、憎いとか…
そんなふうに、十文字以内で答えられるほど、
わたしたちの関係、単純じゃないのかな…？」
findings.todokanai: "Like, dislike, love, hate… is our relationship not simple enough to be described with words like that?"
